On Mon, Jun 20, 2027 at 4:05 PM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Karthik / Neha — forwarding Samir's confirmation on SLOs and burst profile.

Thanks — below are two concrete options and a short streaming note. Numbers are rough order-of-magnitude based on similar workloads.

Option A — Low-latency single-node (fast-path):
- Runtime: dedicate smaller-batch policy, prefer per-request forwarding with max_batch_size=8, aggressive time_slicing (batch wait < 6ms).
- Model: 1x fp16 13B variant with optimized kernels (single model, higher flops).
- Concurrency: scale horizontally on active connection count; target single-request p95 ~ 90–110ms, p99 ~ 180–230ms for 20–80 token outputs.
- Cost estimate: ~$1,200 per 1M tokens (higher due to low batching efficiency).
- Tradeoffs: best latency but higher unit cost; streaming latency minimal since we avoid long batch waits.

Option B — Cost-optimized hybrid (batch + cache + quant):
- Runtime: continuous batching with dynamic batch sizing, prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts, and quantized model path for bulk requests.
- Model variants: quantized 13B (4-bit) for the bulk path + floating 7B fast-path for latency-sensitive tiny requests.
- Concurrency: excellent amortization at steady 50 users—expected p95 ~ 110–150ms, p99 ~ 200–300ms depending on burst behavior.
- Cost estimate: ~$420–650 per 1M tokens (depending on hit rate of KV cache & quantization quality).
- Tradeoffs: lower cost but slightly wider tail; requires careful cache warming and model fallback policy for bursts.

Streaming considerations:
- Batching increases token latency for the first streamed token. To preserve streaming UX, we recommend a hybrid fast-path: requests under X tokens (e.g., <=24 tokens) hit an express path with max_batch_size small and immediate flush; longer requests go through continuous batching.
- KV caching helps reduce compute on repeated prefixes, but caching must be kept per-user or per-session to avoid correctness issues for clinical context.

Trial proposal (what we can validate in a 60-minute run):
- Validate p95/p99 targets at steady 50 concurrency for both options.
- Run 3 burst windows (simulate 250 concurrent for 60–90s) to observe tail behavior and autoscaling reaction.
- Measure streaming first-byte latency under both modes.

I’ll prepare the short PDF proposal with the two configs + estimated costs and a simple runbook for the trial (will attach).
